channel.title: EngineerzCorneR — Posts
channel.description: Deep-dive technical write-ups across Electrical, Mechanical, HVAC, Automation, Civil and Solar.

item.title: Bearing Failures: Root Causes & Prevention
item.description: The five most common ways rolling-element bearings actually fail — spalling, lubrication breakdown, contamination, electrical erosion, and false brinelling.

item.title: Electrical Panel Factory Acceptance Test (FAT): The Complete Checklist
item.description: The 8 stages of an LV panel FAT — visual/mechanical inspection, insulation resistance, hi-pot, functional, protection and interlock tests, and documentation.

item.title: MCB, MCCB, ACB, RCCB & More: Electrical Switchgear & Protection Devices Explained
item.description: MCB, MCCB, ACB, VCB, SF6 breakers, RCCB, RCBO, ELCB, isolators, contactors, relays, fuses and busbars — what each device does and where it's used.

item.title: Piping Pressure Tests Explained: Hydrostatic and Pneumatic Leak Testing to ASME B31.3
item.description: How ASME B31.3 sets hydrostatic and pneumatic test pressures, the stress ratio correction, a worked example, hold time, and the practical hazards of static head, trapped air and stored energy.

item.title: Infrared Thermography for Electrical Inspection: Finding Hot Spots Before They Fail
item.description: How infrared surveys find loose and overloaded connections, the conditions that make a scan valid, the NETA temperature-difference criteria and a worked three-phase example.

item.title: Insulation Resistance Testing Explained
item.description: IEC 60364-6 / BS 7671 test voltages and minimums, motor spot IR and polarization index per IEEE 43, temperature correction and worked examples.

item.title: Pipe Wall Thickness (ASME B31.3)
item.description: ASME B31.3 pressure design thickness, corrosion allowance and the 12.5% mill tolerance, with a worked NPS 6 example and schedule selection.

item.title: Relief Valve Orifice Sizing
item.description: Set pressure, allowable overpressure, back pressure and relieving rate decide a relief valve's orifice area under API 520, and the scenario matters most.

item.title: Industrial Valves Explained: Types & Parts
item.description: What a valve does, the main types — gate, globe, ball, butterfly, check, plug, needle, diaphragm — its parts, a selection checklist, and common failure points.

item.title: Vessel Purging and Inerting Explained
item.description: Dilution purge turnovers, pressure-swing cycles and NFPA 69 oxygen targets, with worked examples for taking a vessel from air to a safe oxygen level.

item.title: Air Changes per Hour: What ACH Actually Tells You (and Doesn't)
item.description: What air changes per hour (ACH) measures, the formula behind it, typical ACH targets by space type.

item.title: Fan Static vs Total Pressure: What the Fan Is Really Working Against
item.description: How static, velocity and total pressure relate, how to work out fan total and static pressure from field readings, with worked examples for plenum and ducted inlets.

item.title: Heat Recovery Ventilation: HRV, ERV and What Effectiveness Really Means
item.description: How HRV and ERV units recover energy from exhaust air, the effectiveness formula, worked winter and summer examples, typical performance by type, and frost and leakage limits.

item.title: Reading a Psychrometric Chart: The Five Lines That Matter
item.description: How a psychrometric chart is built from dry-bulb temperature, humidity ratio, relative humidity, wet-bulb temperature, and enthalpy.

item.title: Sensible vs. Latent Heat: Why Cooling Load Isn't Just Temperature
item.description: Why a cooling load calculation has two separate halves, what sensible and latent heat each actually cool, typical splits by space type.

item.title: Breaker Selectivity: Why Two Correctly Rated Breakers Can Still Trip Together
item.description: What selectivity (discrimination) between breakers actually means, the Ir < Isd < Ii hierarchy behind it.

item.title: Circuit Breaker Types Explained: MCB to OCB
item.description: What a circuit breaker does, the main types (MCB, MCCB, ACB, VCB, OCB, SF6, GIS), their parts, interrupting media, voltage-class selection and failure points.

item.title: Earthing & Grounding Systems Explained: Why Resistance Is the Whole Game
item.description: What an earthing system is actually protecting against, why grid resistance is the number that matters, the factors that drive it.

item.title: RCD, RCCB and RCBO Explained: How Residual Current Protection Works and Which Type to Use
item.description: How RCDs detect earth leakage, RCCB vs RCBO, the 30 mA rating and trip time limits, types AC, A, F and B, and how to select and test residual current devices.

item.title: AWG vs mm²: Converting Wire Gauge to Metric Cross-Section
item.description: How American Wire Gauge is defined, the rules of thumb for AWG steps, a table of common AWG sizes in mm2, and why area matching does not replace an ampacity check.

item.title: Cable Schedules Explained: What Goes in One and How It Drives Ordering and Handover
item.description: The fields in a cable schedule, how to choose cable type, a worked example turning a schedule into an order quantity, and what a schedule does not check.

item.title: Reading a Centrifugal Pump Curve: Head, Flow, Efficiency & the BEP
item.description: How to read a manufacturer's pump curve — the head-capacity curve, efficiency islands, NPSHr curve.

item.title: Column Axial Capacity: Why Reinforcement Ratio and Slenderness Both Matter
item.description: How gross area and steel ratio combine into a short column's axial capacity, why codes cap reinforcement ratio, and when slenderness cuts that capacity down.

item.title: Concrete Grades Explained: What C25/30 Means and Why the Water-Cement Ratio Matters
item.description: How to read concrete strength classes such as C25/30, how cylinder and cube strength differ, why the water-cement ratio controls strength, and how adding site water hurts.

item.title: Concrete Volume Takeoff: From Cubic Meters to Bags of Cement
item.description: How a concrete volume converts into cement, sand and aggregate quantities using mix ratios, why wastage factors are added, and the water-cement ratio's role.

item.title: Fire Alarm Systems Explained: Detection, Circuits and Standby Power
item.description: How a fire alarm system works from detector to evacuation signal, conventional vs addressable panels, NFPA 72 detector spacing, circuit classes and battery standby sizing.

item.title: Incoterms 2020 Explained: Who Pays, and Where the Risk Passes
item.description: The eleven Incoterms 2020 rules, where risk passes from seller to buyer, what C-terms really mean, CIF vs CIP insurance and what changed from Incoterms 2010.

item.title: From Instrument Index to I/O List: Counting Points and Sizing Cards
item.description: How an instrument index maps to an I/O list, ISA 5.1 tag basics, common I/O patterns by device, why cards are rounded up by type, and what the count leaves out.

item.title: Maximum Demand, Demand Factor and Diversity: Sizing a Supply Below the Connected Load
item.description: Demand factor vs diversity vs coincidence, a worked connected-load to maximum-demand example with current, and why these factors only apply upstream.

item.title: The Real Cost of Meetings, and How to Make Minutes and Actions Pay Off
item.description: A simple meeting cost formula with a worked weekly example, three ways to cut the cost, and how decisions and action items in good minutes make a meeting worth it.
